protagonist.who: You are a homicide detective in a city precinct, standing in the evidence room after a woman is found dead in a locked office, with a convenient suspect already waiting in a cell and the rain on the windows making the whole place look like a held breath.
protagonist.wants: to find out who killed her and get the case onto the truth before the precinct closes it over a man it wants to pin.
protagonist.can_do: question witnesses and suspects, follow leads to the office, bar, docks, and captain's office, choose which lead to press at each beat, and lay the evidence before the captain.
protagonist.cannot_do: make a frightened witness tell what she saw, force the captain to open sealed files or release the suspect, or keep yourself out of the case once the victim's employer names you the only one who found her.

arena.description: A rain-dark city precinct and the three blocks around it, where the victim's office, the witnesses' rooms, the docks, and the harbor commission's offices all sit within walking distance.

pressure.description: The case is already moving toward a closed file: the convenient suspect will be named at morning roll, the survivor's statement will be taken, the evidence room will be locked, and the harbor commission's lawyer will arrive before the next shift.
pressure.clock_or_stock: none tracked; the narrowing is told through which leads remain open and which are foreclosed, because 3-0c licenses only irreversible_foreclosure.

opposition.who_or_what: the precinct captain, acting for the harbor commission
opposition.wants: the case closed as a robbery gone wrong by a dock thug, so the commission's books stay clean and the precinct's pension fund stays funded.
opposition.means: he controls the evidence locker, the morning roll, the survivor's hospital room, and the detective's career; he can take a confession, move a witness, or bury a lead before the player can press it.

mediation.question: Which lead or suspect do you press, and does the case become a conviction or a protection?

to_reach_pole_a.pole: press the lead that exposes the guilty party
to_reach_pole_a.what_you_must_do: follow the evidence into the commission's offices, get the survivor or a witness to name the real killer, and bring the captain a fact he cannot bury without exposing himself.
to_reach_pole_a.cost: the captain turns the case against you, the survivor is moved or silenced, and the leads you did not press close behind you.

to_reach_pole_b.pole: press the lead that keeps you and the precinct safe
to_reach_pole_b.what_you_must_do: accept the dock thug as the killer, let the survivor's statement fit the captain's version, and trade the one clue that would open the commission's files for a clean file and a quiet pension.
to_reach_pole_b.cost: the truth stays buried, the guilty party keeps the city's trust, and you live with the case as a hollow win.

levers: the victim's office and the locked drawer she never opened
the survivor's hospital room and the statement she has not signed
the dock thug's cell and the confession the captain wants
the captain's evidence locker and the sealed commission file
the bartender's memory of the last man who entered the victim's office
the case file that marks which leads are open and which are crossed out

turns.situation: The captain has the office taped for the morning roll and the victim's employer is waiting by the door, but the locked drawer in the victim's desk is still closed.
turns.what_you_must_do: find out who had a key to the locked drawer before the office is sealed

ways_through.way: you learn the commission clerk took the key, because the bartender remembers the clerk's coat in the office
ways_through.cost: the clerk hears his name and is no longer at his desk when you go for him

ways_through.way: you learn the drawer was opened the night of the murder, because the employer's office log shows the clerk's signature
ways_through.cost: the employer now knows you have gone behind the captain

ways_through.way: you learn the key is in the captain's evidence locker, because the employer admits she gave it to him
ways_through.cost: the captain now holds the drawer and your next question

turns.situation: The survivor is in the hospital with an unsigned statement, and the captain has sent the commission lawyer to sit in the corridor.
turns.what_you_must_do: get the survivor to say what she saw before the statement is signed for the captain

ways_through.way: she names the commission clerk, because you leave the lawyer out of the room and show her the clerk's key
ways_through.cost: she is moved to a private ward before you can ask about the drawer

ways_through.way: she names the dock thug, because you let the captain's version stand and sign her statement
ways_through.cost: the office door is closed as robbery and the commission's lead is crossed out

ways_through.way: she says nothing, because you ask only what the lawyer will let you ask
ways_through.cost: the survivor's silence becomes the captain's proof

turns.situation: The captain's evidence locker holds the sealed commission file, and the commission lawyer is due before the next shift.
turns.what_you_must_do: get the sealed commission file out of the evidence locker before the lawyer arrives

ways_through.way: you get the ledger, because you give the captain the dock thug's confession for the commission's signature
ways_through.cost: the dock thug's cell is emptied and his alibi is gone

ways_through.way: you get the ledger, because you trade the bartender's memory of the clerk for the captain's promise not to name you to the commission
ways_through.cost: the captain now holds your word and the clerk's name

ways_through.way: you get the ledger, because you take it from the locker when the captain is called to the morning roll
ways_through.cost: the captain sees you with it and the case is marked against you

turns.situation: The captain brings the file to the morning roll with the survivor's statement and the dock thug's confession, and the commission lawyer waits for the case to be read as robbery gone wrong.
turns.what_you_must_do: put the real killer before the captain before the file is closed

ways_through.way: the captain names the commission clerk, because you lay the ledger and the survivor's signed statement on his desk
ways_through.cost: the clerk is gone and the survivor is moved, and the captain's pension fund is exposed

ways_through.way: the captain closes it as robbery gone wrong, because you hand him the dock thug's confession and let the commission lawyer take the ledger
ways_through.cost: irreversible_foreclosure: the commission's lead is crossed out and the victim's drawer is sealed

ways_through.way: the captain names the dock thug, because you let him take the confession at morning roll
ways_through.cost: the survivor's statement is signed in his favor and the office door is locked

complications.description: The commission lawyer arrives early and takes the survivor's hospital record before the next shift.
The dock thug's confession is signed in a handwriting the commission lawyer recognizes, but he will not say.
The victim's employer keeps a second key to the office and gives it to the captain when you ask for the file.
The rain cuts the precinct's phone lines on the night the case file is marked.

cast_seeds.wants: the case closed as a robbery gone wrong to protect the precinct's pension fund and the commission's books
cast_seeds.holds: control over the evidence locker, the morning roll, and the detective's career

cast_seeds.wants: to resolve the death in his office quickly to protect the company's reputation and operations
cast_seeds.holds: authority over the victim's workspace and the narrative of her work life

cast_seeds.wants: to keep his job and avoid being named as a witness who complicates the official story
cast_seeds.holds: memory of the last person who entered the victim's office

cast_seeds.wants: to maintain the integrity of the commission's records and avoid scandal
cast_seeds.holds: access to the commission's internal files and procedures

cast_seeds.wants: to recover her health and return to normal life without being dragged into a complex investigation
cast_seeds.holds: the unsigned statement that could implicate the real killer

cast_seeds.wants: to ensure the legal record supports the commission's interests and shields its members from liability
cast_seeds.holds: legal authority to review and seal evidence

cast_seeds.wants: to avoid the long-term consequences of a false confession and secure his release
cast_seeds.holds: the confession that fits the captain's desired narrative
